content.comment_body: Hello, regarding this topic: I have a [product_name] [article_no]. I connect using an Ethernet cable linked to a USB port with an adapter. Upgrading from Windows 10 to Windows 11 required me to update [product_name] and move from [version_no] to [version_no]. Now, I can’t connect to [product_name] anymore—the communication interface does not find it. The IP addresses are set correctly (192.168.1.47 for the PC and 192.168.1.10 for [product_name]). Has anyone else encountered this issue? On ipconfig, I noticed Ethernet port 3 had IP 169.254.54.239. Should this be the address for [product_name] or for the PC? Thanks for your help.

Hi [user_name], this forum prefers communication in English. Please write your next posts in English. Thanks. Here is your opening post translated: The IP address 169.254.54.239 is the IP of the USB/Ethernet adapter. The adapter uses its own IP, which is not the same as the PC's (192.168.1.47). You need to change the adapter’s IP to match the subnet 192.168.1.x.

Thank you for the quick reply. Since I’m not an IT expert, how do I change the Ethernet IP address? What’s surprising is that with Windows 10, I used the same adapter and never had any issues. Thanks.
Please respond in English as I don't understand French.
Sorry and thank you for your quick response. What surprises me is that with Windows 10, I used the same adapter and had no issues. Thank you.
I'm unable to advise on this.

Ipconfig displays your TCP/IP network configuration, and multiple IPs means your computer is on different networks. If you see 169.254.X.X, it indicates a problem with your network adapter—try reinstalling its driver, check online tutorials for configuration, or visit forums related to network adapters. Another option is to use a network router with Ethernet and WiFi ports, connecting the computer via WiFi and [product_name] by cable.

analysis.insight_summary: The user cannot connect to their [product_name] after upgrading [product_name] and moving from Windows 10 to Windows 11. The issue stems from network adapter configuration, with the device no longer recognized even though the setup previously worked on Windows 10. Contributors suggested checking the network adapter's IP settings to ensure it is within the correct subnet for proper connectivity.
